To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the degree of liver damage caused by ischaemic reperfusion in rats and rabbits was not reduced by inhibitors of the enzyme poly (ADP ribose) synthetase, but was reduced by deferoxamine and tiron, which are radical scavengers.

the liver injury caused in the rat by ischaemia of the liver (60 min) followed by reperfusion (2 h) was not reduced by the administration of the PPARS inhibitors 3‐AB, ISO or 4‐AN before reperfusion, whereas deferoxamine and tiron significantly reduced this injury.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of inhibitors of the enzyme poly (ADP-ribose) synthase (PARS), which is activated by DNA strand breaks caused by reactive oxygen and nitrogen species.
the role of oxygen‐derived radicals in the development of reperfusion liver injury.
the role of oxygen‐derived radicals in the pathogenesis of reperfusion liver injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the liver injury associated to ischaemia and/or reperfusion is not mediated by poly (ADP ribose) synthetase activation.

the generation of ROS is a key event in the liver injury caused in the ischaemic‐reperfused liver, but the mechanism(s) of the generation of these ROS are not yet known and the role of PARS in these mechanisms remains to be determined.
PARS inhibitors are not effective in the protection of the ischaemia‐perfused liver in vivo.

PARS is not a key mediator of liver injury caused either by ischaemia or ischaemia‐ reperfusion.
